title: Dispatch CUS 7: One Council Refuses the Paired Census
summary: The eviction deadline arrives while the overlapping houses begin to tighten.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Alderwick’s council approved the paired census on Wednesday. The council beyond Vesper Row rejected it by one vote, fearing it would grant permanent legal force to doors they did not choose to open. Its Office of Improvements has not withdrawn the notices, although Miss Hume says no officer intends to carry them out.

The new entries in Alderwick’s volume stabilized the North Loom storeroom. On the other side, cracks appeared above three Vesper Row doors as the rejected wording remained unchanged. Dr. Saye warns that the two arrangements may settle by damaging whatever stands across their boundary.

Miss Hume has returned with a certified copy of the vote and a request for another hearing. She says her council could accept a limited entry stating that the other city is real for census purposes without settling any question of property. Miss Morrow and Alderman Dorne have agreed to that wording.

Mr. Keene packed the books nearest the doorway. Ada Keene moved her daughter’s furniture back from it. They have spoken each day, but neither asks the other to leave a home. “I will not take the house in which she raised a child,” he said. Mrs. Keene answered that she will not ask him to surrender the shop he built after his wife died.
The alternate council meets tonight. Inspector Voss has placed wardens at the shared addresses until the vote is known. Residents have been told to sleep away from the affected walls.
